Answer: B
Reason: The CT scan (Figure 1a) clearly demonstrates a sharp foreign body (fishbone) penetrating the esophageal wall with adjacent extraluminal air, indicating esophageal perforation. In the context of circulatory collapse and this imaging finding, pneumothorax (or hydropneumothorax) is the most likely direct complication among the choices, as opposed to simple effusion or isolated pneumomediastinum which do not fully capture the severity implied by the perforation and clinical state. Although Figure 2 appears relatively clear, the definitive pathology is shown in Figure 1a.
